summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 (Phala Testnet TEE Migration) to migrate the TEE worker from root into apps/tee-worker/, integrate shared monorepo packages, add Phala Cloud CVM deployment, and ship the feature via PR.
summary.outcome: All 6 plans completed across 4 waves, CVM deployed to Phala Cloud production infra (not testnet), 58 tests passing, security review conducted with all high/medium findings fixed, PR #395 created and reviewed.

repo: Phala Cloud has no separate testnet — the free tier ($20 credit) runs on the same production nodes (Intel TDX hardware, prod5 cluster) as paid deployments. Phase naming 'phala-testnet' was a misnomer.
The entire branch stores full conversation transcripts as JSONL files and is pushed automatically by the checkpoint system — any credentials shared in conversation will appear in transcript commits.

SSRF validation in ssrf-validation.ts originally had a TOCTOU DNS rebinding vulnerability — DNS lookup happened separately from the HTTP fetch, allowing DNS rebinding attacks against cloud metadata endpoints.
The migration-worker's SSRF check was comparing the wrong variable: `endpoint !== 'cipherbox'` should be `protocol !== 'cipherbox'` for the cipherbox:// protocol guard.
gsd-tools init uses the current working directory — when executing from the main repo while plans exist only in a worktree, phase_found returns false. Must run gsd-tools from the worktree directory.
Parallel agent worktrees can cause git config lock conflicts — sequential execution avoids this when waves have only 2 plans.
The deploy-staging.yml workflow has build-tee and deploy-tee-phala jobs that handle full CVM rebuild and redeploy on staging-v* tag push, reading secrets from GitHub staging environment.
multiformats (CID.parse) is already a dependency of @cipherbox/crypto and is the correct way to validate CIDs — rolling a regex for CIDv0/CIDv1 detection is unnecessary and incomplete.
undici is bundled with Node.js but requires explicit installation as a dependency for TypeScript type resolution in pnpm workspaces.

code.finding: Was calling getKeypair() instead of getPublicKey(), leaking private key into route scope — a critical security bug caught in simplify review.
Was reading TEE_EPOCH env var but migrate route uses TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH — inconsistency caused wrong epoch to be reported in health endpoint.
Using req.path for unmatched routes causes unbounded Prometheus label cardinality. Fixed to '/:unmatched' (consistent with API's http-metrics.interceptor.ts:40 pattern).

Original DNS pinning via hostname rewrite broke TLS SNI/certificate validation. Fixed to use undici Agent with custom lookup function that resolves DNS once and pins the IP while preserving original hostname for SNI.
Epoch assignment using ?? parseInt(process.env.TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH || '1', 10) can yield NaN if env var is non-numeric. Fixed to validate with Number.isNaN and fall back to 1.

teePrivateKey.fill(0) only ran in the CID-loop finally block — if decryptEcies or validateEndpointUrl threw during setup, the key was never zeroed. Fixed by wrapping entire function body in try/finally.

decryptEcies trusted encryptedHex without validation — Buffer.from('invalid', 'hex') silently produces truncated buffer. Added explicit hex validation (non-empty, even length, /^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/) before passing to unwrapKey.
FetchFn type was exported from ./types but not re-exported from the public index, forcing consumers to use ProviderOptions['fetchFn'] or deep imports.

workflow: Pause/resume across machines works well with /gsd:pause-work + /gsd:resume-work — HANDOFF.json preserves credentials, task state, and next actions for the receiving session.
Credentials shared in conversation should be rotated after the session — they appear in entire-branch transcript checkpoints even if deleted from planning files.
After rotating secrets in GitHub, the next staging-v* tag push automatically rebuilds and redeploys with new credentials — no manual CVM intervention needed.

Security review (security:review command) followed by /simplify is an effective pre-PR cleanup sequence — caught the getKeypair/getPublicKey bug, metrics label cardinality, and epoch env var inconsistency.
CodeRabbit caught the TLS SNI hostname-rewrite issue that security review missed — automated PR review is complementary to pre-commit review.
Checking `gh secret list --env staging --json name,updatedAt` provides timestamps to confirm secret rotation completed.

friction: Usage limit interruption mid-wave-2 parallel execution — had to continue the session and retry both Wave 2 agents sequentially.
Git config lock conflicts when running agents in parallel with worktrees — Wave 2 had to fall back to sequential execution.
gsd-tools init returned phase_found: false when run from main repo while branch was checked out in a worktree — required switching to worktree context.
STATE.md merge conflicts appeared after every agent worktree merge — needed manual resolution each time.
undici type resolution failed in pnpm workspaces even after explicit install — required moving to a static import and explicit dependency declaration.
Handoff HANDOFF.json stored credentials (Phala API key, TEE worker secret) in plaintext — these were committed to git history and required rotation.
Docker wasn't available on the development machine — needed to coordinate image build on the Docker host (192.168.133.12) via session transfer.
HANDOFF.json from pause-work contained stale info about an 'uncommitted Dockerfile fix' that had already been committed — caused brief confusion on resume.
open_items: CVM is running on Phala Cloud production infra under $20 free tier credit — no cost monitoring or alert set up for credit exhaustion.
Phase directory name '35-phala-testnet-tee-migration' remains as a misnomer since renaming would break cross-references — docs clarify but name persists.
Connection probe deduplication (connection-test.ts vs sdk-core probe logic) was identified as a refactor candidate but deferred — flagged as tech debt.
The entire-branch transcript at 86/0546ed796e/0/full.jsonl contains the old (now-rotated) Phala API key and TEE worker secret — the values are inert post-rotation but the history is not scrubbed.
Republish latency at ~1155ms avg is network-bound to Phala Cloud testnet from dev machine — production co-location numbers not yet measured.
HUMAN-UAT.md persists with status: partial for the 2 human-verified items (CVM health, GitHub secrets) — will surface in /gsd:progress until explicitly closed via /gsd:verify-work.

Sequential batch processing in republish route was flagged for potential parallelization but deferred as a deliberate security tradeoff — should be revisited with explicit documentation of the tradeoff.
